column13: Replaces TS20P03G (20A/200V). GBU8J is only rated 8A continuous vs the 15A F1 fuse rating - verify actual motor current stays well under this before relying on it.

My aluminum case provides the heatsink for Q1 ( drive mosfet ) and MOTOR_FLYBACK. If you do not have a case that can act as a big heatsink, these two components will need a fairly decent sized heatsink(s). I also have a smaller heatsink on BR1 ( the bridge rectifier )
T2/T3/T4 removed - replaced by IC2 (MIC4422) gate driver. T1 remains - it drives the REV MOSFET via OK2, unrelated to the motor gate drive.

Replaces discrete T2/T3/T4/R5/R18 push-pull driver. PLACEHOLDER WIRED in Driver1: IC2 is currently an LM393 DIP-8 symbol (no exact MIC4422 part in library) standing in for the real part - swap the symbol/footprint for a real MIC4422YN before fabrication. Wired as: +IN1->PWM net, -IN1->GND (reference), OUT1->old gate-drive node (feeds DRV_0/Q1 gate network and LED1), VCC->+12V, GND->GND. Add a 0.1-1uF ceramic decoupling cap from VCC to GND next to the IC.
Could use other relay, even with solder leads - the plug in relays work well with connectors terminated by female 1/4" fully insulated quick disconnects
